title: The Price Tag Code
covers: converting between equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents using hundredths and benchmark values
cert: writing equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents for the same value

intro.caption: Lesson 4-2 — relate fractions, decimals, and percentages. The limited-edition sneakers are locked in the back-room safe, and the sticky note with the code went missing. Only three price tags remain.

balloons.t: The vault keypad wants three percents. All we have are three weird tags.
I did NOT eat the sticky note. Stop looking at me.
First tag says 13/20. Easy — 13 percent, right?
Wrong! That's 13 out of 20. Scale the bottom to 100 first.
Tag two says 0.08! That's definitely 80 percent!
0.8 is 80 percent. 0.08 is eight hundredths. Check the place value!
Fractions, decimals, and percents are three outfits for the same number.
Wait, so 3/4, 0.75, and 75% are all the exact same score?
Can't open your own safe? I'll buy the whole locked box for ten bucks.
Keep walking, Sly. We've got the code.
Golden sneakers! Now THAT is a 100 percent certified drop.

win.caption: Every fraction, decimal, and percent in an equivalent set names the same value. Scale denominators to 100, and multiply decimals by 100.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Fraction to Percent
gates.prompt: Turn each fraction tag into an equivalent fraction out of 100 to read its percent.
hints: Conceptual: percent means out of 100, so a fraction gives its percent once the denominator is 100.
Procedural: multiply both the numerator and denominator by the same number so the denominator becomes 100.

steps: Multiply 5 by 20 to get 100, so multiply 3 by 20 too: 3 × 20 = 60.

fb.msg: 13% is 13 out of 100, not 13 out of 20. Multiply both terms by 5.
20 is the denominator. Scale 20 up to 100.
26 doubled 13, which only scales 20 to 40. Multiply by 5 to reach 100.

items.q: Another tag shows 3/4. Which fraction out of 100 and percent match 3/4?

options.fb: 3/4 is not 34/100. Multiply both 3 and 4 by 25.

gates.pass: 65% and 75% locked in. Cole nods — he will never read 13/20 as 13% again.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Decimal to Percent
gates.prompt: Ruben thinks 0.08 is 80%. Use place value and hundredths to decode the decimal tags.
hints: Conceptual: hundredths sit two places after the decimal point. 0.08 is 8 hundredths (8/100), while 0.80 is 80 hundredths (80/100).
Procedural: multiply the decimal by 100 (slide the decimal point two places right) to get the percent.

steps: The 4 is in the hundredths place, so 0.04 = 4/100.
Slide the decimal two places right: 0.04 × 100 = 4%.

items.q: Tag two reads 0.08. Ruben yells 80%. What is 0.08 as a percent?

options.fb: 80% is 0.8 or 0.80. In 0.08, the 8 is in the hundredths place, so it is 8%.
Move the decimal point two places right, not one: 0.08 × 100 = 8%.

items.label: A backup tag reads 0.45. Percent = (%)
items.aria: percent equivalent to zero point four five

fb.msg: Move the decimal point two places right, not one.
0.45 is still the decimal. Multiply by 100 to write the percent.

items.fbDefault: 0.45 is 45 hundredths, which is 45 out of 100.

gates.pass: 8% and 45%! Hye-jin taps her glasses — her calculator agrees.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Match All Three
gates.prompt: Match equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents — and compare two values written in different forms.
hints: Conceptual: equivalent forms name the exact same part of a whole, just written in different ways.
Procedural: rewrite every number in the same form (like percents) before you match or compare them.

worked.q: Write 1/4 as a decimal and a percent.

items.q: Which set shows three equivalent forms of the same value?
Cole's tag says 0.7 and Tasha's says 3/4. Which value is greater?

gates.pass: Three forms matched! Only the final safe dials remain.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Crack the Safe
gates.prompt: Enter all three dials to open the sneaker safe before Sly tries another lowball offer.
hints: Conceptual: scale fractions to 100, and read decimals in hundredths.
Procedural: multiply fraction terms so the bottom is 100; multiply decimals by 100.

fb.msg: 9 is out of 20, not 100. Multiply both terms by 5.
18 doubled 9, which only makes 40 on the bottom. Multiply by 5.

items.label: Dial 2 · Convert 0.05 to a percent. (%)
items.aria: percent equivalent to zero point zero five

fb.msg: 50% is 0.5 or 0.50. 0.05 is 5 hundredths, which is 5%.
Slide the decimal two places right: 0.05 × 100 = 5.

items.q: Dial 3 · Which trio is 100% equivalent and opens the final lock?

options.fb: 17/20 is not 17/100. Multiply both terms by 5 to get 85/100.

gates.pass: CLICK-CLANK! 45%, 5%, and 85%! The safe door swings wide and Sly slinks out.

journal.heading: Lesson 4-2 — what the price tag code taught us
rows: Scale both top and bottom so the denominator becomes 100: 13/20 = 65/100 = 65%.
Multiply by 100 (move the decimal two places right): 0.08 = 8%, while 0.80 = 80%.
To compare 0.7 and 3/4, turn both into percents first: 70% vs. 75%.
0.08 is 8 hundredths (8%), not 80%. Always check the hundredths place.
journal.quote: "Three tags, one number, zero excuses." — Hye-jin

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 4-2 (Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. Covers converting fractions and decimals to percents and comparing equivalent forms.
standards: Write equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents for the same value
